newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens in volatile market.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens in volatile market.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling fell against the dollar on Friday on demand from importers mainly in the energy sector, commercial bank dealers said.
While supply held steady, importers had rushed into the market fearing dollar/shilling rates might go too high and driven dollar rates high, they said.
Central Bank of Kenya posted a commercial mean rate of 54.85 against the dollar, compared with 53.75 on Thursday.
Against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 89.04 from 87.47.
"We're jumping 50 cents and sometimes more when quoting in the interbank, when before we only used to move between 20 and 10 cents," one dealer said.
Another dealer said they were maintaining wide spreads of about one shilling.
"It's a mixture of two things. Yesterday, there was genuine demand but I think a lot of what's happenning now is also (due to) a lot of speculation," another said.
Dealers said this was the first time the central bank had stayed out of the market for such a time -- three weeks -- and some players were caught offguard in uncomfortably long dollar positions.

"(Central bank) participation in the market used to hold rates within a certain level and guide the market by providing ceilings, but now no-one wants to be caught in any position because they do not know the next turning," one dealer said.
The money market was tight. Overnight rates were quoted at 23 percent, almost unchanged.
